doctrine:
LIGHTING_SET_UPS_OG CONSOLIDATED DOCTRINE

SOURCE QUALITY NOTE: Document is ~88% transcribed YouTube/podcast/tutorial boilerplate with sponsored sidebars (Milanote, moodboarding tools). Actionable content is ~10-12% of total word count. No SNIPED-specific apparatus configs or composite environment rotation setups present. What follows is the full extracted operating knowledge, de-duplicated.

---

1. PORTRAIT STUDIO SETUP (only SNIPED-adjacent hardware reference in document)
- Three-strobe portfolio: Profoto D2 key + Westcott Optical Spot accent + gobo for shadow control + fill
- Gel shadow behavior: gels shift shadow color independently of highlight zone; exploit for separation
- Tethered raw workflow: shoot tethered, show client final image quality on laptop before they leave (mandatory confidence-builder)
- Model direction via reference images: show the image, not the instruction

2. NINE PORTRAIT LIGHTING PATTERNS (reference grid)
- Split: light 90 degrees to side, half face lit, half shadow
- Rim: light from behind/side, outlines subject, separates from background
- Butterfly (paramount): light directly above and in front, creates butterfly shadow under nose
- Clamshell: two lights above and below subject axis, kills shadows, popular for beauty
- Loop: light slightly above eye level, offset, creates small loop shadow from nose
- Rembrandt: light angled so triangle of light appears on shadow-side cheek
- Short: key light on narrow (far) side of face; slims face
- Broad: key light on wide (near) side of face; widens face
- Cross: two lights from opposite sides at same angle, used for texture and drama

3. LIGHT QUALITY AND BEHAVIOR FUNDAMENTALS
- Quality (hard vs soft): determined by source size RELATIVE to subject distance. Larger source or closer = softer
- Inverse-square law: light intensity drops by square of distance. Doubling distance cuts power to 1/4
- Diffusion: scatter the beam (bag, scrim, modifier) to soften transitions
- Feathering: aim the edge of a light source at subject rather than center; exploits the falloff gradient for more even, natural-looking spread. Default headshot tactic: parallel feathered lights, one each side, perpendicular to ground
- Color isolation: colored gels on separate light sources allow independent control of background vs subject color
- Dynamic range constraint: cameras capture 13-15 stops vs human eye 21-24 stops; expose for highlights, recover shadows in post; never trust in-camera preview in blown-out ambient

4. LIGHT DIRECTION THEORY (clock-model framework)
- Visualize: camera at 6 o'clock, subject at center, light source hours represent angle around face
- Front light (6 o'clock): flat, low drama, even coverage
- Side light (3 or 9 o'clock): maximum shadow drama, reveals texture
- Back light (12 o'clock): rim/separation; requires fill or reflector on front
- Intermediate positions (4-5 or 7-8 o'clock): loop/Rembrandt zone; most common editorial compromise

5. NATURAL LIGHT TIMING
- Golden hour: 1 hour after sunrise, 1 hour before sunset; warm directional, long shadow, high texture contrast
- Blue hour: 1 hour before sunrise, 1 hour after sunset; soft blue-tinted ambient, low contrast, minimal harsh shadow; optimal for clean environmental portraits without supplemental strobe
- Midday: hard overhead, raccoon eyes, unflattering for faces; requires shade or diffusion panel
- Overcast: giant softbox, flat, low drama; best for color accuracy and even skin rendering

6. JAWLINE AND POSING MECHANICS (universal, all body types)
- Turtle move: neck forward, chin slightly down; sharpens jawline, reduces double-chin without instruction that sounds critical
- Teach as a neutral technical cue, not a corrective one

7. SUBJECT CONNECTION AND EXPRESSION PROTOCOL
- Expression is the bottleneck, not lighting perfection
- Gear hierarchy: expression first -> connection + disarm technique -> lighting
- Disarm tactics: kids/pets small talk, calibrated banter, forget-the-camera presence, show final image tethered to build trust loop
- Parallel lighting + tethering is the minimum viable headshot environment for subject comfort

8. WHAT THIS DOCUMENT DOES NOT CONTAIN
- SNIPED composite environment rotation lighting configs
- Apparatus-layer lighting doctrine
- Profoto D2 power-setting specifics per environment
- Location scouting x lighting interaction
- Any AI-composite lighting matching methodology

CAPABILITY NOTE: Clock-model (6 o'clock camera frame) is a clean pedagogical tool reusable in SNIPED apparatus design docs and onboarding materials. Feathering + parallel setup is the safe default for any headshot booking. Blue hour timing constraint applies directly to outdoor composite environment shoots.
